## Why This Exists

## Original Index-Language Anchor

IX-060.md is the central Acer-side anchor. It records the index-language interpretation: IX/LX entries act as vocabulary, chains act as sentence paths, and the catalog is the dictionary. It also preserves the Liris insight and the early about-12:1 token-compression family.

That maps directly to Jesse's operator-provided original chain-language example:

`	ext
@from [liris] machine [lx 1] time[1-24-2026] ask [ix-1] (acer) tool [eds18] skill [38] run program [1873]
`

Read as an index language, that sentence is not a prose note. It is a tuple route: origin seat, machine lane, time coordinate, target IX concept, peer machine, tool number, skill number, and executable program number.
